div.head: II Cn 5.1
div.ab: Hæðenscipe byð, þæt man deofolgyld weorðige, þæt is þæt man weorþige hæðene godas ⁊ sunnan oððe monan, fyr oððe flod, wæterwyllas oððe stanas oððe æniges cynnes wúdutreowa, oððon wiccecræft lufige oððon morðweorc gefremme on ænige wisan, oððon on blote oððon fyrhte, oððon swylcra gedwimera ænig þíngc dreoge.

[Þæt] bið þæt man idol weorðige, hæ[þ]ne godas ⁊ sunnan oððe monan, fyr oððe flod, wǽterwyllas oððe stanas oððe æniges cynnes wudutréowa, oððe wiccecræft lufie oððe morðweorc gefremme on ænige wisan, oððe on blote oððe on fyrhte, oððe swylcra gedwímera ænig ðing dreoge.

Hæðenscype byð, þæt man idola weorðige, þæt is þæt mann weorðige haðene godas ⁊ sunnan oððe monan, fyr oððe flod, wæterwyllas oððe stanas oððe æniges cynnes weodatreowa, oððe wiccancræft lufige oððe morðweorc gefremme on ænige wysan, oððe on hlotæ oððe fyrhte, oððe on swylcra gedwymera ænig þing dreoge.

Gentilitas est, si quis idola colat, id est gentilium deos, solem aut lunam, ignem uel fluctus, aquas fontium uel lapides uel alicuius generis ligna, uel picceancreft (incantationis artem) diligat aut murdri opus quolibet modo sectetur aut in sacrificio (id est secundum ritum Suuanorum) — uel mortificia quoquo modo suscipiat aut in sorte — uel in fyrhte uel in similibus fantasiis (uel prestigiaturis) aliquid agat.

uidelicet colere idola, solem, lunam, ignem, aquam, fontes, lapides, lignum frondosum, lignum uiride aut aridum adorare, maleficia exercere, morthrum amare; hęc (enim) omnia omni Christiano ex parte Dei prohibemus.

Paganissimus quippe est, ut quis idola colat, scilicet paganos deos, solem et lunam, ignem uel flumen, fontes et saxa siue cuiusquam generis arborem aut ueneficium diligat seu homicidium furtiuum efficiat ullo modo siue in sanguine uel in transmigracione uel in talibus erroribus quicquam factitet.

Þæt bið þæt man idol weorðige, hæþne godas ⁊ sunnan oððe monan, fyr oððe flod, wǽterwyllas oððe stanas oððe æniges cynnes wudutréowa, oððe wiccecræft lufie, oððe morðweorc gefremme on ænige wisan, oððe on blote oððe on fyrhte, oððe swylcra gedwímera ænig ðing dreoge.

Hæðenscipe byð þæt man deofolgyld weorðige, þæt is þæt man weorþige hæðene godas and sunnan oððe monan, fyr oððe flod, wæterwyllas oððe stanas oððe æniges cynnes wudutreowa, oððon wiccecræft lufige oððon morðweorc gefremme on ænige wisan, oððon on blote oððon fyrhte, oððon swylcra gedwimera ænig þingc dreoge.

Heidenthum (Das B) ist, dass man Götzen verehrt, nämlich dass man heidnische Götter verehrt und Sonne oder Mond, Feuer oder Fluth, Wasserquellen oder Steine oder Waldbäume irgend welcher Art, oder Hexenkunst pflegt oder heimliche Mordstiftung übt auf irgend welche Weise, entweder in Opferdienst (Loosbefragen A) oder (in B) Zukunftschauen, oder irgend etwas von solcherlei Trugbildern vollzieht.

Heathenism (That, B) is, that one worships idols, namely that one worships heathen gods and the sun or moon, fire or flood, springs or stones or forest trees of any kind, or practises witchcraft, or commits secret murder in any way, either by sacrifice (by casting lots, A) or (by, B) divination, or carries out anything of such delusions.

Namely, the worship of idols, heathen gods, and the sun or the moon, fire or water, springs or stones or any kind of forest trees, or indulgence in witchcraft, or the compassing of death in any way, either by sacrifice or by divination or by the practice of any such delusions.

It is heathen practice if one worships idols, namely if one worships heathen gods and the sun or the moon, fire or flood, wells or stones or any kind of forest trees, or if one practises witchcraft or encompasses death by any means, either by sacrifice or divination, or takes any part in such delusions.

Heathen practices are devil worship, that is, the worshipping of heathen gods, of the sun or the moon, of fire or water, or of springs or stones or any type of tree; the devotion to witchcraft or conspiring to bring about a person’s death by any means, either through sacrifice or divination or by engaging in any other similar idiocies.

Ducange s. v. caragus; Brotanek Texte Altengl. Lit. 107. 125, übs. ins Agsä. ebd. 20); Ähnliches übt hier Einfluss

Used by Northu 48. Cf. Gl Heidentum 4—6a. 8. An English preacher of the 10th cent. has fures, falsi testes, ad arbores, fontes vota reddentes, qui caragios, divinos, præcantatores inquirunt (ed. Ducange s. v. caragus; Brotanek Texte Altengl. Lit. 107. 125, translated into A.-S. ibid. 20); something similar exerts an influence here

Vgl. Gl Baum 1. Da Baumstümpfe oft in Urkk. Grenzpunkte bezeichnen, erhielt man sie vielleicht in einer ursprünglich religiösen Ehrfurcht.—‘Hollunder und verschiedene andere’ Can. Edg.
Cf. Gl Baum 1. Since tree-stumps often mark boundary points in charters, they were perhaps preserved out of what was originally religious reverence. — ‘Elder and various others’ Can. Edg.

Dass hlote (sorte Q; vielleicht hierher hlot Northu 48 ed. Spelman) nicht bloss Schreibfehler, bemerkte K. Maurer in Kr. Üb. V 216 richtig. Über Losrunen bei heidnischen Germanen s. Mogk in Paul Grundr. Germ. Philol. 1080. 1133f.; Grimm Dt. Mythol.² 989. 1064.—Blutzauber hat Cons im Sinne, wenn er sanguine schreibt, indem er blode las oder zu lesen meinte

That hlote (sorte Q; perhaps hlot Northu 48 ed. Spelman belongs here) is not a mere scribal error was rightly noted by K. Maurer in Kr. Üb. V 216. On lot-runes among the heathen Germanic peoples see Mogk in Paul Grundr. Germ. Philol. 1080. 1133f.; Grimm Dt. Mythol.² 989. 1064. — Cons has blood-magic in mind when he writes sanguine, having read, or believed he read, blode
Nicht ‘facula, Kerze, Fackel’ oder fyrhto (Furcht), wie Frühere verstanden. Vgl. Wb: freht, frihtrung: hariolatio (Sweet Old. texts 512);’frihtere: Weissager; Gl: Wahrsagung
Not ‘facula, candle, torch’ or fyrhto (fear), as earlier scholars understood it. Cf. Wb: freht, frihtrung: hariolatio (Sweet Old. texts 512); ’frihtere: soothsayer; Gl: Wahrsagung

See Bede, ed. Plummer, ii. p. 59 f., for a list of the references in Bede and elsewhere to heathen practices such as idolatry, sacrifices, etc. Idolatry was first forbidden by law by Erconbert of Kent (640–664), see Bede, Lib. iii. ch. 8, while Wihtred also inflicts penalties upon those who make offerings to devils (see cap. 12 f.). No further references to heathen practices appear in the Laws until the period of the Danish settlement, cf. V Atr. 1 and note. References to the worship of idols, divination, etc. appear also in Poen. Theod. 27 (ed. Thorpe, Anc. Laws, ii. pp. 32–4); Poen. Egb. ii. 22, iv. 19 (ibid. pp. 190, 210); Dial. Egb. xv. (ibid. p. 94); Can. Edg. 16 (ibid. p. 248); Wulfstan, pp. 12, 303; N.P.L. 48; 54.
For the use of this expression in apparently heathen poetry see Hákonarmál, Strophe 21, ed. Kershaw, A.S. and Norse Poems, p. 108.

on blote, G, B; on hlotæ, A. Q has in sacrificio…in sorte, apparently translating both. Two texts of Q add after sacrificio (id est secundum ritum Suuanorum). For the continuation of heathen observances in Sweden after the kings had become Christian see Kershaw, Stories and Ballads, p. 141 ad fin., also Heimskr., Saga Sigurðar, Eysteins ok Olafs, Chap. 28; Adam of Bremen, iv. Ch. 26 f.
Cf. Norse frett, an inquiry of gods or men about the future.
